scenes.visual: WDollar — the ep11 particle $1, frozen mid-form; bottom-bar counter fades in: REVENUE $0.00
scenes.text: Eleven episodes. Nine products live on the internet. A fleet of AI workers running day and night. And in all that time, this company has not been paid one single dollar by anyone. That counter at the bottom has never moved.

scenes.visual: particles drift; the counter holds; a faint wallet outline appears under the $
scenes.text: Tonight it can. Not because we found a customer. Because we finally finished the one thing a company needs before any customer can pay it — a way to get paid that nobody else controls.

scenes.visual: one particle breaks loose and drops into the wallet — soft chime, cut to black
scenes.text: This is the episode where the first money has to appear.

scenes.visual: WStakes — stakes card over dark room; no title repeat
scenes.text: And if it doesn't, you'll watch exactly why. Same rule as always. Real numbers. Real failures. No staging.

scenes.visual: WNewCrew — tool cards land one by one: Claude Code · Codex · Kimi · Zcode · Hermes · GrokBot; chapter whoosh
scenes.text: Before the money — what changed. In the last few months, AI moved faster than this channel could film it. Dan's workbench today is Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Zcode, Hermes and GrokBot. Each one does a job that used to take a week of wiring. Together, they're the reason this company moves at all.

scenes.visual: WRebuilt — OpenClaw card dims and slides out, Hermes card takes its place; then the droplet map redraws: four droplets → two: "DEXTER — the video machine", "NANO — NervixPay ops"
scenes.text: And some things had to go. OpenClaw — the system this fleet was born on — was costing more time than it saved. Hermes replaced it. The droplet agents were redesigned from scratch: two machines now, and each one works on exactly one priority. Dexter runs the video machine. Nano runs NervixPay operations. No busywork. No agents running just because they exist.

scenes.visual: WWhy — the new crew converges on one word: SHIP
scenes.text: That rebuild is how the next thing got finished so fast. Because the most important thing this company built since last episode isn't another product. It's the way every product gets paid.

scenes.visual: WTurn — the ep11 line on screen, struck through in red: "Stripe is not wired yet"
scenes.text: First, a correction. Last episode I told you we'd wire up Stripe on camera. I changed my mind. Not because Stripe is bad. Because of what it means to put somebody else's gate between your customer and your money.

scenes.visual: WLandlord — a toll gate between two wallets; five gates slam one by one with labels
scenes.text: A payment processor has to approve you. It can hold your payouts for days. It takes a percentage of every sale — around three percent, plus a fee on top. A customer can reverse a payment weeks later. And on a bad day, it can close the account. Five gates. Every one of them belongs to someone else.

scenes.visual: WOwnRail — SiteFrame: nervixpay.live live; chapter whoosh
scenes.text: So the fleet built its own. This is NervixPay — live at nervix pay dot live. A checkout that takes payment straight from the customer's wallet into the merchant's wallet. It never holds the money. It can't freeze it. It can't move it. It only does one job: prove, on the blockchain itself, that the payment really happened.

scenes.visual: WInstant — three cards: "No approval queue" · "Sell the same day" · "Nobody can switch it off"
scenes.text: And here's why that matters for a company like this one. When we build a product, we don't wait for anyone to say yes. We make a link, and we can sell it that afternoon. No application. No underwriting. No landlord.

scenes.visual: WForYou — the share panel: checkout link, QR code, embed snippet
scenes.text: And it's not only for us. Any business can use it. A website, a consultant, a shop, a service. You connect a wallet, you name a price, you get a link, a QR code, or a snippet for your site. That's the whole setup.

scenes.visual: WStable — a flat line labelled "1 USDC = $1" vs a jagged line labelled "volatile crypto" (schematic)
scenes.text: Now — why crypto? Because people hear 'crypto' and think of a coin that doubles on Monday and halves on Friday. That's not what we take. We take stablecoins. USDC and USDT. One coin is one dollar. Today, tomorrow, next year. It's not a bet. It's a dollar that moves like an email.

scenes.visual: WNoBank — the old path collapses: customer → card network → processor → bank → merchant, "two to three days" → one arrow: customer wallet → merchant wallet, "minutes"
scenes.text: Look at what disappears. No bank in the middle. No card network taking its cut. No chargebacks. No waiting until Tuesday for Friday's money. It settles in minutes, on a Sunday night, across any border. That's why I think this is the future of money — not because it's new. Because it's simpler.

scenes.visual: WAgentMoney — Hermes, Dexter, Nano cards: "open a bank account" ✗ ✗ ✗ → "receive USDC" ✓ ✓ ✓
scenes.text: And for this company there's one more reason — the biggest one. Our workers are AI agents. An agent cannot open a bank account. It has no passport, no signature, no branch to walk into. But it can hold a wallet. For an AI company, stablecoins aren't the fancy option. They're the only money our workers can actually touch.

scenes.visual: WHonestDeps — checklist: what we still depend on
scenes.text: Full honesty. 'No third party' isn't perfectly true. We still depend on the blockchain to run, and on the companies that issue those coins. Customers pay a small network fee. And NervixPay charges merchants a flat monthly plan — ten dollars to start. A flat fee. Never a percentage of your sale. Nobody stands between the customer and the money.

scenes.visual: WSetup — real UI captures in SiteFrame: sign in → connect wallet → sign once → "Ownership verified"; top-right THE RAIL appears with a pointer sign
scenes.text: Here's the rail, end to end. That panel in the corner lights one segment at a time, only when you've seen it work. A merchant signs in and connects the wallet they already use. They sign once to prove it's theirs. No money moves. They create a product, and they get a link. LINK lights.

scenes.visual: WScan — phone: checkout, pick USDC on Polygon, exact amount + QR, confirm in wallet → SCAN lights → confirmations 1-2-3 → VERIFIED ON-CHAIN lights → dashboard row, "Paid directly to your wallet" → IN THE WALLET lights
scenes.text: The customer opens the link, picks a coin and a network, scans, and confirms in their own wallet. NervixPay doesn't take their word for it. It reads the chain itself, finds the exact amount, and only then marks it paid. And the money is already where it belongs — in the merchant's wallet. Four segments. Lit.

scenes.visual: WReceipts — three ledger rows stamp in with block numbers; each gets a red stamp: TEST — NOT REVENUE
scenes.text: Has it ever actually worked? Yes — three times, and here are the receipts. The twenty-fourth of September: one cent's worth of TON. The twenty-sixth: three dollars in USDC on Polygon. And the same day, a ten dollar Starter plan, paid in USDC, certified end to end. And here's why the counter didn't move: every one of those came from a wallet we control. That's plumbing. Not revenue.

scenes.visual: WAudit — SiteFrame: the 12 October audit, verdict line highlighted; nine-row grade table
scenes.text: On the twelfth of October the fleet audited the whole thing. Nine hundred and twelve tests passing. Zero errors in production for a week. And the verdict, in its own words: not ready for a public launch yet — ready for a controlled beta with invited merchants, once two blockers are closed. A legal page. And a second source to double-check the blockchain. Since then, the legal pages have gone live. The second source is still on the list — so for now, the beta stays invite only.

scenes.visual: WMoment — the season so far in one line: products ✓ · rail ✓ · audit ✓ · customer ☐ — the empty box pulses
scenes.text: So this is the moment. Eleven episodes building. A rail we own. A product that works. An audit that says we're ready to invite the first merchants. There's exactly one box left on this list — and nobody inside this company can tick it. The first money has to come from outside. And it has to come now.

scenes.visual: WOffer — the offer card: NERVIXPAY STARTER · 10 USDC · INVITED BETA; beta link chip pointing to the description
scenes.text: Here's the offer. A NervixPay Starter plan. Ten dollars, in USDC, paid through NervixPay itself, straight into the company wallet. The payment product earns its first money through its own rail. The first merchants are invited — if you run a business and want a seat in the beta, the link is in the description. The counter is live. Let's see if it moves.

scenes.visual: WLands — real dashboard row from an outside wallet; the bottom-bar counter POPS $0.00 → the real invoice amount; chime
scenes.text: And there it is. An invited merchant — not us, not a test wallet — a ten dollar Starter plan, paid in USDC, verified on the chain, sitting in the company wallet. Eleven episodes of zero. And the first dollar this company ever earned arrived in money an AI can hold, on rails we built ourselves.

scenes.visual: WFails — the counter holds at $0.00; the empty box flashes red
scenes.text: And — not yet. The invitations went out, and no merchant has paid. The rail works, and you've seen it work. What's missing isn't code. It's a customer. That's the honest result, and it's the job of the next episode.

scenes.visual: WHuman — 90/10 echo from ep10 and ep11
scenes.text: The fleet wrote the rail. It tested it, audited it, and fixed what the audit found. But it couldn't decide that this company would never rent its cash register from somebody else. That was a human choice. Like a poker player refusing a table where the house can change the rules mid-hand. The ten percent. Again.

scenes.visual: WNext — the promise card; the counter stays on screen
scenes.text: One dollar isn't a business. It's a door opening. Next episode: the open launch — and the first stranger who finds this company through the flywheel and pays because the product was worth it. The counter stays on screen from now on. It never resets.

scenes.text: This was DansLab, number twelve. The First Dollar. If you want to see that counter climb — subscribe, and hit like. You'll be here when it happens. Build. Ship. Repeat.
